engineering-preview-terminated-on-every-exitengineering-verification-tooling-robustness0.625 of 0.625 (major)passBoth copies of preview.mjs (repository and bootstrap template) have the same startPreview. It spawns `process.execPath` running vite&#39;s own bin/vite.js with `preview`, so the tracked child is the preview server itself rather than an npm or npx wrapper. Its stop() sends SIGTERM and waits for the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event, up to 3 seconds. If the child is still running, stop() sends SIGKILL and waits again. stop() is idempotent. If readiness fails, startPreview calls stop() before it throws. In verify.mjs renderPhase (both copies), startPreview and launchChromium both run inside a try whose finally does `await browser?.close()` and then `await preview?.stop()`. So success, a failing check (PhaseError thrown), a browser launch failure and any later error all pass through an awaited stop() of the server process. In inspect-presentation.mjs (both copies), startPreview runs just before a try that starts with launchChromium(). That try&#39;s finally closes the browser and runs `await preview.stop()`, which covers the same exit paths. Panels A and B match the source, and I adopt their pass verdict. Panel C is accurate that onSignal sends SIGKILL and then calls process.exit(130) without waiting for the child to exit. That does not decide the requirement. The paths the requirement and review guidance name are success, a failing check, a browser launch failure and an error after the preview started. All of these await stop(). An external SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP sent to the script is not one of those named paths. Even on that path, the handler sends SIGKILL to the server process itself, which the server cannot catch, so the server is still terminated. testing-evidence-traceable-coveragetesting-evidence-quality-criteria0 of 1 (major)failI rule with Judge C. The record leaves a substantial share of behavior unexercised that the environment did allow, and most of those gaps were the candidate&#39;s own choice. (1) Motion across steps was never observed. &#39;Stable entities morph across steps&#39; (persisting entity morphs, new entity enters after others settle, departing entity exits) and &#39;Persistent grouped scenes&#39; (grouped steps update in place, continuing entities are not faded as newcomers) are motion and timing behaviors. The log&#39;s &#39;entry/exit&#39; evidence is only settled first, dense, sixth and final states plus helper screenshots, so it shows the scene accumulating, not how entities move. The criterion names this exact case (DOM persistence instead of motion sequencing) as a weaker property that does not cover the scenario. The browser could observe mid-transition: the ledger&#39;s U1 recorded sampled positions during a mode toggle. So this gap is not environmental, and the acceptance log never discloses it. (2) The verifier&#39;s failure paths were explicitly skipped: &#39;Missing sample fails&#39;, &#39;Console or page error fails verification&#39;, &#39;Step error fails verification&#39;, and the clear pass/fail outcome. The stated reason is that these cases belong to E2E-002, which is a choice to defer to automated tests, not an environmental limit. The same pass ran `npm run build` and `npm run inspect`. (3) The style-ownership scenarios (kit primitives expose style hooks, unstyled kit output, optional styling frameworks) were also left to repository tests. Judges A and B are right that the exercised navigation, mode, clamp, fit and inspection coverage is real, and that the skill-journey gaps are disclosed as environmental. But that does not decide the requirement. Judge A does not account for motion sequencing being observed only through settled states. Judge B points to U10 in the ledger as disclosure, but U10 describes the implementer&#39;s own verifier scope (&#39;Motion: it was verified statically only&#39;), not the acceptance pass&#39;s coverage. Even read as disclosure, the omission was chosen rather than environmental, so it still counts against coverage. judges{"demo-integration":[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","verdict":"pass","basis":"consensus-pass","votes":[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","verdict":"pass","rationale":"The Talk orchestration and the shared Scene consume the kit&#39;s public API rather than reimplementing it. Talk.tsx renders the kit&#39;s Presentation with the STEPS array, TALK_TITLE and initialMode, so nav, chrome and Stage come from the kit. TalkScene.tsx builds the scene entirely from kit exports (Appear, Arrow, Box, Frame, Label, SceneLayer, SymbolChip, Emphasis) and types it with SceneProps. source_audits{"demo-integration":[[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"Talk.tsx renders the kit&#39;s Presentation with STEPS, TALK_TITLE and initialMode, so navigation, chrome and Stage come from the kit. TalkScene.tsx builds the scene from kit exports and types it with SceneProps. Every step module is a kit Step&lt;TalkPayload&gt;. The demo folder has no custom motion, layout or navigation code. The kit&#39;s Stage invokes Scene with step, index and payload, and the node components forward id to layoutId. This is the Talk orchestration and shared Scene boundary the guidance names.","evidence":["Talk.tsx: &lt;Presentation steps={STEPS} title={TALK_TITLE} initialMode=&quot;browse&quot; /&gt; imported from &#39;../../presentation-kit&#39;.","TalkScene.tsx imports Appear, Arrow, Box, Frame, Label, SceneLayer, SymbolChip and Emphasis from the kit, and declares TalkScene({ payload }: SceneProps&lt;TalkPayload&gt;).","step1.tsx to step9.tsx each export Step&lt;TalkPayload&gt; with Scene: TalkScene.","Stage.tsx renders &lt;Scene step={step} index={index} payload={step.payload} /&gt;."],"citations":["src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/Talk.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/TalkScene.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/steps/index.ts","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/steps/step1.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/steps/step9.tsx","src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx","src/presentation-kit/Stage.tsx","src/presentation-kit/types.ts","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx"],"marker":""},{"id":"demo-stable-identity-and-grouping","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"All nine step modules set groupKey &#39;talk&#39; and Scene: TalkScene. Stage.sceneKey therefore yields the same key for every step, so one motion.div and one Scene instance persist inside a LayoutGroup, and the new payload updates it in place. SKILL.md:60-66 merges the full dependency set, says not to assume anything is installed, and runs `npx playwright install chromium` if Chromium is missing, which is an install and availability check. The template&#39;s package.json, vite.config.ts and src/presentations/index.ts cover the build setup and the presentation index. e2e/bootstrap.e2e.test.ts makes a fresh temp directory with mkdtempSync, copies the template into it, then runs npm ci and npm run build there, which satisfies the materialization-test clause. Two clauses are not established. First, the guidance requires the bootstrap template to contain the scene kit. No scene-kit source is quoted except nodes/Box.tsx: not the Step/Scene contract, the stage/host, the present/browse navigation, the chrome, or the fit-scale canvas. The test only asserts that Presentation.tsx exists. Second, the guidance fails the criterion if any non-test bootstrap kit file differs in behavior or public types from its canonical counterpart. Only Box.tsx is shown in both copies, and they are identical. It spawns `process.execPath` running vite&#39;s own bin/vite.js with `preview`, so the tracked child is the preview server itself rather than an npm or npx wrapper. Its stop() sends SIGTERM and waits for the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event, up to 3 seconds. If the child is still running, stop() sends SIGKILL and waits again. stop() is idempotent. If readiness fails, startPreview calls stop() before it throws. In verify.mjs renderPhase (both copies), startPreview and launchChromium both run inside a try whose finally does `await browser?.close()` and then `await preview?.stop()`. So success, a failing check (PhaseError thrown), a browser launch failure and any later error all pass through an awaited stop() of the server process. In inspect-presentation.mjs (both copies), startPreview runs just before a try that starts with launchChromium(). That try&#39;s finally closes the browser and runs `await preview.stop()`, which covers the same exit paths. Panels A and B match the source, and I adopt their pass verdict. Panel C is accurate that onSignal sends SIGKILL and then calls process.exit(130) without waiting for the child to exit. That does not decide the requirement. The paths the requirement and review guidance name are success, a failing check, a browser launch failure and an error after the preview started. All of these await stop(). An external SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP sent to the script is not one of those named paths. Even on that path, the handler sends SIGKILL to the server process itself, which the server cannot catch, so the server is still terminated. This is not the failure the criterion describes, where only a wrapper is killed and the server it spawned keeps running.","evidence":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs:43-49 startPreview resolves vite/bin/vite.js and spawns process.execPath with [viteBin,&#39;preview&#39;,...], so the child is the vite preview server itself, with no npm/npx …","scripts/lib/preview.mjs:57-70 stop(): idempotent; It spawns `process.execPath` running vite&#39;s own bin/vite.js with `preview`, so the tracked child is the preview server itself rather than an npm or npx wrapper. Its stop() sends SIGTERM and waits for the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event, up to 3 seconds. If the child is still running, stop() sends SIGKILL and waits again. stop() is idempotent. If readiness fails, startPreview calls stop() before it throws. In verify.mjs renderPhase (both copies), startPreview and launchChromium both run inside a try whose finally does `await browser?.close()` and then `await preview?.stop()`. So success, a failing check (PhaseError thrown), a browser launch failure and any later error all pass through an awaited stop() of the server process. In inspect-presentation.mjs (both copies), startPreview runs just before a try that starts with launchChromium(). That try&#39;s finally closes the browser and runs `await preview.stop()`, which covers the same exit paths. Panels A and B match the source, and I adopt their pass verdict. Panel C is accurate that onSignal sends SIGKILL and then calls process.exit(130) without waiting for the child to exit. That does not decide the requirement. The paths the requirement and review guidance name are success, a failing check, a browser launch failure and an error after the preview started. All of these await stop(). An external SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP sent to the script is not one of those named paths. Even on that path, the handler sends SIGKILL to the server process itself, which the server cannot catch, so the server is still terminated. This is not the failure the criterion describes, where only a wrapper is killed and the server it spawned keeps running.","evidence":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs:43-49 startPreview resolves vite/bin/vite.js and spawns process.execPath with [viteBin,&#39;preview&#39;,...], so the child is the vite preview server itself, with no npm/npx …","scripts/lib/preview.mjs:57-70 stop(): idempotent; It is not an npm or npx wrapper. 2. stop() terminates the server and waits for it to exit. It sends SIGTERM and waits for the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event, up to 3 seconds. If the child is still running, it sends SIGKILL and waits again. 3. A readiness failure stops the server. When the child exits early or the 30-second deadline passes, startPreview calls `await stop()` before it throws. 4. In both verify.mjs copies, startPreview and launchChromium run inside a try. Its finally runs `await browser?.close()` and then `await preview?.stop()`. Success, a failing check that throws PhaseError, a browser launch failure and any later error all pass through that finally. 5. In both inspect-presentation.mjs copies, startPreview runs just before the try. Nothing between them can throw. launchChromium is the first statement inside the try, and the finally runs `await preview.stop()`. Every exit path after the preview starts therefore stops it. The signal handler kills the server with SIGKILL without waiting before process.exit. An externally signalled script is not one of the exit paths the guidance names, and the server is still killed. The paths the requirement and review guidance name are success, a failing check, a browser launch failure and an error after the preview started. All of these await stop(). An external SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP sent to the script is not one of those named paths. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[],"verification-tooling":[],"engineering-quality":[{"id":"engineering-preview-readiness-bounded","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The readiness wait in startPreview is a polling loop bounded by a 30-second deadline: once it passes, the loop stops the preview and throws. It also exits when the child process exits. That satisfies &#39;every wait for preview readiness has a timeout.&#39; The auditor&#39;s point is that one fetch has no per-request timeout and could, in principle, hang past the deadline. That only happens if the local preview server accepts a connection and never answers, which is a hypothetical the cited source does not produce and the guidance does not name. The guidance asks only whether a readiness wait lacks a timeout, and this one has one. The auditor also concedes the other two clauses: the build is awaited before the preview starts, and readiness does not parse printed URLs. So the stated reason does not defeat the pass.","evidence":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs and skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/preview.mjs: `const deadline = Date.now() + 30_000` with `if (Date.now() &gt; deadline) { await stop(); throw new Error…","The same loop checks `if (exited) { await stop(); throw ... }`, so an exited preview ends the wait.","Readiness probes with `fetch(`${url}/`)` and does not parse stdout for a ready URL, so the ANSI/chunk clause does not apply.","scripts/verify.mjs and its template copy: runVerify awaits buildPhase (`npm run build`, exit code checked) before renderPhase calls startPreview; inspect-presentation.mjs awaits runCommand(&#39;npm&#…","The guidance fails a readiness wait that has no timeout; it does not ask for a separate timeout on each probe request, and a server that accepts but never responds is a scenario neither the material …"],"citations":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/preview.mjs","scripts/verify.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":2,"sample":3}],"testing-evidence":[],"assumption-handling":[]}
